options: Lets some light through, looks blurry
Lets light through so you see clearly
transparent.hint: The answer is "Lets light through so you see clearly". Transparent things let light pass through and you can see clearly through them.

options: Transparent means the same as opaque
A clear glass window lets sunlight in
transparent.hint: The answer is "A clear glass window lets sunlight in". Clear glass is transparent, so light passes through it.

transparent.q: Fill in the blank: A transparent material lets light ____, and you can see clearly through it.
transparent.hint: The answer is "pass through". Light passes through transparent materials.

transparent.q: What is the word for a material you can see clearly through?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Transparent". Transparent materials let light through so things look clear.

transparent.q: Which kind of material lets the MOST light pass through?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Transparent". Transparent lets light through, translucent lets only some, and opaque lets none.

transparent.q: Which is an example of a transparent material?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Air". You can see clearly through air, so it is transparent.
The answer is "A wood board". Wood blocks light, so it is opaque, not transparent.
The answer is "Clear glass, air, plastic wrap". Clear glass, air, and plastic wrap all let light through clearly.

transparent.q: Which item belongs with clear glass and air?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Plastic wrap". Plastic wrap is transparent, just like clear glass and air.
The answer is "A clear drinking glass". You can see clearly through a clear glass.

transparent.q: Mia wants to cover leftovers and still see the food clearly. What should she use?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Plastic wrap". Plastic wrap is transparent, so you can see clearly through it.

transparent.q: Sam shines a flashlight at a clear glass window. What happens to the light?
transparent.hint: The answer is "It passes through the glass". Clear glass is transparent, so light passes through.

transparent.q: A pet store wants a fish tank so people can see the fish clearly. What is the best material?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Clear glass". Clear glass is transparent, so you can see the fish clearly.

transparent.q: At a science fair, Leo holds plastic wrap, wax paper, and a wood block in front of a lamp. Through which can he see the lamp clearly?
transparent.hint: The answer is "Plastic wrap". Plastic wrap is transparent; wax paper is blurry and wood blocks light.

transparent.q: Why can you see the playground through the classroom window?
options: Clear glass lets light pass through
transparent.hint: The answer is "Clear glass lets light pass through". Clear glass is transparent, so light passes through it.

options: Lets light through; things look clear
Lets some light through; things look blurry
translucent.hint: The answer is "Lets some light through; things look blurry". Translucent things let some light through, so things behind look blurry.

translucent.q: What is the word for a material that lets some light through but makes things look blurry?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Translucent". Translucent means some light passes through and things look blurry.

translucent.q: Fill in the blank: A translucent material lets ____ light pass through.
translucent.hint: The answer is "some". Translucent materials let only some light through.

options: Translucent lets less light through than transparent
Translucent blocks more light than opaque
Translucent means the same as opaque
translucent.hint: The answer is "Translucent lets less light through than transparent". Transparent lets light through, translucent only some, opaque none.

translucent.q: You look at a friend through a translucent sheet. What do you see?
translucent.hint: The answer is "A blurry shape". Translucent materials make things on the other side look blurry.

translucent.q: Which is an example of a translucent material?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Wax paper". Wax paper lets some light through and makes things look blurry.
The answer is "A metal pan". Metal blocks all light, so it is opaque.
The answer is "Wax paper, frosted paper". Wax paper and frosted paper let some light through and look blurry.

translucent.q: Which item belongs with wax paper?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Frosted paper". Frosted paper is translucent, like wax paper.
The answer is "A frosted glass window". Frosted glass lets some light in but things look blurry.

translucent.q: Ava wants a lamp shade that lets some light out but hides the shape of the bulb. Which is best?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Frosted paper". Frosted paper is translucent, so some light gets through but the bulb looks blurry.

translucent.q: Ben tapes wax paper over a flashlight and shines it at the wall. What does he see?
options: Light just as bright as before
A dimmer glow on the wall
translucent.hint: The answer is "A dimmer glow on the wall". Wax paper is translucent, so only some light gets through.

translucent.q: At a science fair, Zoe looks at a toy through clear glass, wax paper, and a wood block. Which makes the toy look blurry?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Wax paper". Wax paper is translucent, so things behind it look blurry.

translucent.q: Kai covers a window with frosted paper. What happens in the room?
translucent.hint: The answer is "Some light still comes in". Frosted paper is translucent, so it lets some light through.

translucent.q: Why does a toy look fuzzy behind wax paper?
options: Wax paper makes its own light
translucent.hint: The answer is "Only some light gets through". Translucent wax paper lets some light through, so things look blurry.

opaque.hint: The answer is "Blocks all light". Opaque materials block light completely.

opaque.q: What is the word for a material that no light can pass through?
opaque.hint: The answer is "Opaque". Opaque materials let no light pass through.

opaque.q: Fill in the blank: An opaque material ____ light completely.
opaque.hint: The answer is "blocks". Opaque materials block light completely.

opaque.q: Which statement is true about opaque materials?
options: You cannot see what is behind them
You can see clearly through them
They make things look a little blurry
opaque.hint: The answer is "You cannot see what is behind them". No light passes through opaque things, so you cannot see behind them.

opaque.q: Which kind of material lets the LEAST light pass through?
opaque.hint: The answer is "Opaque". Opaque materials let no light through at all.

opaque.q: Which is an example of an opaque material?
opaque.hint: The answer is "Brick". Brick blocks all light, so it is opaque.
The answer is "Plastic wrap". Plastic wrap is transparent; light passes through it.
The answer is "Wood, metal, brick". Wood, metal, and brick all block light completely.

opaque.q: Which item belongs with wood and metal?
opaque.hint: The answer is "Brick". Brick is opaque, like wood and metal.

opaque.q: Which thing on the playground is opaque?
opaque.hint: The answer is "A metal slide". Metal blocks all light, so a metal slide is opaque.

opaque.q: Lily wants to block ALL the sunlight from her window so she can nap. What should she use?
opaque.hint: The answer is "A wooden board". Wood is opaque, so it blocks all light.

opaque.q: Max shines a flashlight at a brick wall. What happens to the light?
opaque.hint: The answer is "No light passes through". Brick is opaque, so it blocks light completely.

opaque.q: At a science fair, which item makes the darkest shadow under a lamp?
opaque.hint: The answer is "A metal plate". A metal plate is opaque and blocks all the light.

opaque.q: Why can't you see your friend behind a closed wooden door?
opaque.hint: The answer is "Wood blocks all light". Wood is opaque, so no light passes through it.

opaque.q: You want to hide a surprise gift so nobody can see it. Which container should you use?
opaque.hint: The answer is "A metal tin". Metal is opaque, so no one can see what is inside.

options: From cooler objects to warmer objects
From warmer objects to cooler objects
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "From warmer objects to cooler objects". Heat always flows from warmer to cooler.

heatconduct.q: What is a good conductor of heat?
options: A material that lets heat pass through easily
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "A material that lets heat pass through easily". Good conductors of heat let heat pass through easily.

heatconduct.q: Heat is another name for which kind of energy?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "Thermal energy". Heat is thermal energy.

options: Plastic is a good conductor of heat
Wood is a good conductor of heat
Metals are good conductors of heat
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "Metals are good conductors of heat". Metals let heat pass through easily; wood and plastic do not.

heatconduct.q: What do we call a material that does NOT let heat pass through easily?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "A bad conductor of heat". Bad conductors of heat, like wood and plastic, do not let heat pass easily.

heatconduct.q: Which is a good conductor of heat?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "A metal spoon". Metal is a good conductor of heat.

heatconduct.q: Which is a bad conductor of heat?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "A wooden spoon". Wood does not let heat pass through easily.

heatconduct.q: Which group is ALL good conductors of heat?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "Iron, copper, steel". Iron, copper, and steel are all metals, and metals conduct heat well.

heatconduct.q: Which item belongs with a wooden spoon as a bad conductor of heat?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "A plastic spatula". Plastic, like wood, is a bad conductor of heat.

heatconduct.q: Which part of a cooking pot is made to be a bad conductor of heat?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "The plastic handle". Plastic is a bad conductor, so the handle stays cooler to touch.

heatconduct.q: You hold an ice cube in your warm hand. Which way does the heat move?
options: From the ice to your hand
From your hand to the ice
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "From your hand to the ice". Heat flows from the warmer hand to the cooler ice.

heatconduct.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot quickly?
options: Metal is a good conductor of heat
Metal is a bad conductor of heat
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "Metal is a good conductor of heat". Metal lets heat pass through easily from the soup.

heatconduct.q: You touch a metal slide on a cold morning. Why does it feel cold?
options: Cold moves from the metal into your hand
Heat moves from your hand into the metal
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "Heat moves from your hand into the metal". Heat flows from warmer to cooler, and metal carries it away fast.

heatconduct.q: A cup of hot cocoa sits on the table. What happens over time?
options: It cools as heat moves into the cooler air
It gets hotter from the air
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "It cools as heat moves into the cooler air". Heat flows from the warmer cocoa to the cooler air.

heatconduct.q: In class, Kim puts a metal, a wooden, and a plastic spoon in hot water. Which handle gets warm first?
heatconduct.hint: The answer is "The metal spoon". Metal is a good conductor of heat; wood and plastic are not.

vibration.hint: The answer is "Matter vibrating". Sound happens when matter vibrates.
The answer is "Move quickly back and forth". To vibrate is to move quickly back and forth.

vibration.q: Fill in the blank: Sound travels in ____.
vibration.hint: The answer is "waves". Sound travels in waves.

vibration.q: Which statement is true about air particles when sound travels?
options: They vibrate in place and bump their neighbors
They fly all the way to your ear
vibration.hint: The answer is "They vibrate in place and bump their neighbors". Particles pass the energy along; they do not travel with the wave.

vibration.q: What is the word for moving quickly back and forth?
vibration.hint: The answer is "Vibrating". Vibrating means moving quickly back and forth.

vibration.q: Which is an example of something vibrating to make sound?
vibration.hint: The answer is "A plucked guitar string". A plucked guitar string moves back and forth, making sound.

vibration.q: Which is NOT an example of vibrating to make sound?
options: A book resting on a desk
vibration.hint: The answer is "A book resting on a desk". A resting book is not moving back and forth, so it makes no sound.

vibration.q: Which group ALL vibrate when they make sound?
options: A sunbeam, a mirror, a guitar string
Drum skin, a shadow, a rainbow
Drum skin, guitar string, vocal cords
vibration.hint: The answer is "Drum skin, guitar string, vocal cords". Drum skins, strings, and vocal cords all vibrate to make sound.

vibration.q: Which belongs with a ringing bell and a beating drum?
vibration.hint: The answer is "A twanging rubber band". A twanging rubber band vibrates and makes sound, like a bell and drum.

vibration.q: What part of your body vibrates when you talk?
vibration.hint: The answer is "Your vocal cords". Your vocal cords in your throat vibrate to make your voice.

vibration.q: Jay snaps a stretched rubber band. Why does it make a sound?
vibration.hint: The answer is "It vibrates back and forth". The rubber band vibrates, and vibrating matter makes sound.

vibration.q: You touch your throat while you hum. What do you feel?
vibration.hint: The answer is "Buzzing vibrations". Humming makes your vocal cords vibrate.

vibration.q: At a science fair, rice on a drum jumps when the drum is hit. What does this show?
vibration.hint: The answer is "The drum skin vibrates". The drum skin moves quickly back and forth, making the rice bounce.

vibration.q: After plucking a guitar string, you press it still with your finger. What happens to the sound?
vibration.hint: The answer is "It stops". No vibration means no sound.

vibration.q: Ms. Park strikes a tuning fork and dips its tips in water. What happens?
vibration.hint: The answer is "The water splashes". The vibrating fork shakes the water.

volume.q: What is the volume of a sound?
options: How high or low it is
How loud or soft it is
volume.hint: The answer is "How loud or soft it is". Volume tells how loud or soft a sound is.

volume.q: Fill in the blank: A louder sound has ____ energy.
volume.hint: The answer is "more". More energy means a louder sound.

volume.q: What is the word for how loud or soft a sound is?
volume.hint: The answer is "Volume". Volume is how loud or soft a sound is.

options: Volume is a property of sound
Volume means how hot something is
Volume is a kind of light
volume.hint: The answer is "Volume is a property of sound". Volume is a property of sound.

volume.q: Compared with a shout, a soft whisper has ____ energy.
volume.hint: The answer is "less". Softer sounds have less energy.

volume.q: Which sound has the highest volume?
volume.hint: The answer is "A fire truck siren". A siren is very loud, so it has high volume.
The answer is "A pencil writing on paper". A pencil on paper is a very soft sound.

volume.q: Which list goes from softest to loudest?
volume.hint: The answer is "Whisper, talking, shouting". A whisper is softest and a shout is loudest.

volume.q: Which is an example of using a LOW volume?
volume.hint: The answer is "Whispering in the library". Whispering is a soft sound with low volume.

volume.q: Which belongs with a shout and a siren as a LOUD sound?
volume.hint: The answer is "A thunder clap". Thunder is very loud, like a shout or a siren.

volume.q: Nora taps a drum gently, then hits it hard. How does the second sound compare?
volume.hint: The answer is "It is louder". Hitting harder gives the sound more energy, so it is louder.

volume.q: Why does hitting a drum harder make a louder sound?
volume.hint: The answer is "The sound gets more energy". More energy means a louder sound.

volume.q: Your baby brother is sleeping. What should you do with the TV?
volume.hint: The answer is "Turn the volume down". Turning the volume down makes the sound softer.

volume.q: Pia plucks a guitar string very gently. How can she make the sound louder?
volume.hint: The answer is "Pluck it harder". Plucking harder gives the sound more energy, so it is louder.

volume.q: At a science fair, Eli drops the same ball onto a table from low and from high. Which drop is louder?
volume.hint: The answer is "The high drop". The high drop hits with more energy, so the sound is louder.

medium.hint: The answer is "A material sound travels through". A medium is a material that sound waves travel through.
The answer is "Solids". Particles in solids are packed most closely, so sound is fastest.
The answer is "Gases". Gas particles are spread out, so sound is slowest in gases.

medium.q: Can sound travel through empty space?
medium.hint: The answer is "No, there is no medium". With no medium, there is no sound.

medium.q: Fill in the blank: Sound travels fastest in solids because the particles are ____.
medium.hint: The answer is "packed more closely". Closely packed particles pass the sound along faster.

medium.q: Which is a LIQUID medium for sound?
medium.hint: The answer is "Water". Water is a liquid, and sound can travel through it.

medium.q: Which is a SOLID medium for sound?
medium.hint: The answer is "A wooden table". A wooden table is a solid that sound can travel through.

medium.q: Which is NOT a medium that sound can travel through?
medium.hint: The answer is "Empty space". Empty space has no matter, so sound cannot travel through it.

medium.q: Which list goes from SLOWEST to FASTEST for sound?
medium.hint: The answer is "Air, water, steel". Sound is slowest in gas, faster in liquid, fastest in solid.

medium.q: Which group has a gas, a liquid, AND a solid medium?
medium.hint: The answer is "Air, water, wood". Air is a gas, water is a liquid, and wood is a solid.

medium.q: Astronauts on the Moon need radios to talk. Why can't they hear each other's voices?
options: There is no air to carry sound
medium.hint: The answer is "There is no air to carry sound". Without a medium like air, there is no sound.

medium.q: You put your ear on a desk while a friend taps the far end. Compared with through the air, the sound travels...
options: not at all through the desk
medium.hint: The answer is "faster through the desk". Sound travels faster through solids than through gases.

medium.q: At the swimming pool, does sound travel faster through the pool water or the air?
medium.hint: The answer is "The pool water". Sound travels faster through liquids than through gases.

medium.q: Two cups are joined by a tight string to make a toy phone. What carries the sound between the cups?
medium.hint: The answer is "The tight string". The string is a solid medium that carries the sound.

medium.q: A bell rings inside a jar. Then all the air is pumped out. What happens to the sound?
medium.hint: The answer is "It fades away". With no air as a medium, the sound cannot travel.

options: A material that blocks electrical energy
A material that lets electrical energy pass easily
conductor.hint: The answer is "A material that lets electrical energy pass easily". Conductors let electrical energy pass through easily.

options: Water is a strong conductor of electricity
conductor.hint: The answer is "Water is a strong conductor of electricity". Water is a strong electrical conductor.

conductor.q: Fill in the blank: Metals are ____ conductors of electricity.
conductor.hint: The answer is "good". Metals let electricity pass through easily.

conductor.q: What is the word for a material that lets electrical energy pass through easily?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Conductor". A conductor lets electrical energy pass through easily.

conductor.q: Pencil "lead" conducts electricity. What is it really made of?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Graphite". Pencil lead is graphite, a good conductor.

conductor.q: Which is a good electrical conductor?
conductor.hint: The answer is "A metal paper clip". Metal is a good conductor of electricity.

conductor.q: Which is NOT a good electrical conductor?
conductor.hint: The answer is "A glass marble". Glass is an insulator, not a conductor.

conductor.q: Which group is ALL electrical conductors?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Metal, graphite, water". Metal, graphite, and water all let electricity pass through.

conductor.q: Which item belongs with a steel nail and aluminum foil?
conductor.hint: The answer is "A metal coin". A metal coin is a conductor, like the nail and the foil.

conductor.q: Which part of an electric cord is the conductor?
conductor.hint: The answer is "The metal wire inside". The metal wire carries the electricity; plastic and rubber are insulators.

conductor.q: Ana puts a metal spoon across the gap in a bulb circuit. What happens?
conductor.hint: The answer is "The bulb lights up". Metal is a conductor, so electricity flows to the bulb.

conductor.q: Why should you never use a hair dryer near a filled bathtub?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Water is a strong conductor". Water conducts electricity well, which is dangerous.

conductor.q: At a science fair, Leo draws a thick pencil line, adds it to a circuit, and the bulb lights up. Why?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Graphite is a conductor". Graphite (pencil lead) is a good conductor, so electricity flows through the line.

conductor.q: Which item could close a broken circuit so a buzzer sounds?
conductor.hint: The answer is "A strip of aluminum foil". Aluminum foil is metal, so it conducts electricity.

conductor.q: In a flashlight, metal strips touch the battery and the bulb. What do the strips do?
conductor.hint: The answer is "Carry electricity to the bulb". Metal strips are conductors that let electricity flow.
